name: oily rain puddle in a churned muddy hollow on the ground with tyre ruts, a rainbow sheen and sky reflections
label: wasteland_ruins/puddle
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (1/4)

surfaces.part: puddle with muddy hollow and ruts, seen from above as a flat patch

answer.evidence: The object is an irregular roundish blob, 15 rows tall and up to 15 px wide, with a width profile of 2, 8, 12, 13, 14, 15... narrowing to 4 at the bottom. The column scans show a dark blue water area with sheen and reflection pixels, surrounded by brown mud. There is no vertical south face, no front-edge line and no eave shadow. It lies flat on the ground and is seen from above, which matches the flat kind, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a tiny round vignette of roughly 15x12 source pixels, well under one 16x16 tile. A 4x3-tile ground patch should tile and fill about 64x48. The references are seamless fields of grass and paving texture, while the candidate is an isolated disc with a dark rim, which gives the 'sticker' look. The measured facts (17 visible tones, 0% near-flat coverage) beat the references, but 17 tones on such a small piece comes from packing colour into a small area and not from ground texture. The 29% near-neutral dark edge pixels fit a mixed outline, with some tinted pixels and some near-black. The rim is a separate dark line, not a dark tone of the adjacent material. Inside, the puddle shows a sheen and a few mud tones, about 4 lightness steps against the 5-6 of the Beodeul materials. The mud hollow, tyre ruts and surrounding ground are barely readable. It does not work as a 4x3 ground surface patch, so it fails.

answer.evidence: The object is a roughly circular, irregular puddle seen from above. The silhouette widens from 2 px at row 1 to 15 px at rows 6-10, then narrows to 4 px at row 15, which is the outline of a flat patch of ground. The column scan shows water, sheen and mud colour bands with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical face. It has no front face of 3 or more rows. This is a flat ground decal, so it reads as a top-down slab, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small round vignette, roughly 1.5 tiles across at 2x, with a dark rim, a brown mud ring and a blue puddle centre. It is not a continuous 4x3-tile ground patch like the grass and paving references, which tile edge to edge with grain and tufts or stones shaded one by one. The measured 17 tones per tile and 0% flat coverage are not reliable here. They come from compressing a whole object into one tile, and the tile reads as an icon, not as ground texture. 29% neutral dark edge pixels shows a mixed outline: part tinted brown, part near-black. The rim looks like a sticker outline around an isolated object on a transparent background. The ruts, rainbow sheen and sky reflections are not readable at this size. The mud ring has only about 3-4 steps and little grain, which is shallower than the roughly 5-6 steps of the references. The piece is far too small and sticker-like next to the full-tile references, so it fails.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate does not read as a 4x3-tile ground patch. It is a tiny, roughly 16px round vignette sitting on a dark backdrop, while the references are full seamless surfaces that fill their tiles edge to edge. Its dark rim looks like a closed outline around the whole shape, which is the 'sticker' look rather than a ground surface blending into its surroundings. The 17 visible tones per tile and 0% flat coverage are above both references (3 and 7). But the piece is so small that those numbers come from a few pixels of puddle, rim and sheen packed into one tile, not from ground texture like tufts, soil grain or churned ruts. The mud ramp looks shallow, at about 3-4 steps. The tyre ruts and the churned hollow are not legible at this size. 29% near-neutral dark edge pixels suggests some tinted edges, but the outline still looks mixed. By eye it would look thinner and more sticker-like beside the reference, and it is the wrong size and kind of asset.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small round puddle roughly one tile in size, with a dark rim all the way round it. It reads as an isolated sticker or icon, not a 4x3-tile ground patch that blends into surrounding soil. There are no mud-hollow edges, no tyre ruts spread across the area, and no ground grain around the puddle. The measured facts are fine: 17 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, 0% near-flat coverage, and 29% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is partly tinted and partly neutral. Even so, the shading ramps look shallow, about 4 steps, with the sheen and reflections packed into a tiny disc. The piece fails on kind and structure, not on density.
